mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 5% over three consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of corporate cash flows, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during periods when FEDFUNDS > 5% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of >2% YoY decline in GDPC1.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 4% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE > 4% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for three consecutive months signals contraction in economic output, which depresses earnings and equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during three-month INDPRO declines.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) for two consecutive months indicates a broad-based weakening in demand, which reduces corporate revenue and earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both decline for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both GDPC1 and HOUST decline for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp reduction in the federal funds rate below 2% combined with a concurrent rise in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) above 4% signals a policy-lag environment where monetary easing is insufficient to offset inflation, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as markets anticipate future rate hikes.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when FEDFUNDS < 2% and CPIAUCSL > 4%.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of more than 1% month-over-month for two consecutive months signals a strong labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate profitability, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > previous month +1% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during two consecutive months of >1% monthly PAYEMS growth.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in real retail sales (RSAFS) above trend for four consecutive months signals strengthening consumer demand, which increases corporate revenue and profit expectations, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days regardless of regime.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive during four consecutive months of above-trend RSAFS growth.
